text:
maria: quick heads-up — PR #4321 made our h100-smoke job go red on warmup. Failing with Xid 79 + 'invalid device function'. job: https://ci.internal.redwood/12345 :eyes:

ci-bot: Build 12345 - h100-smoke - FAILED (warmup)

jack: ugh. any log snippet? did the PR touch native kernels or CUDA flags?

maria: minimal change (rdw-infer: bump attention kernel threshold). here's tail of runtime log:
```
[2026-03-17T14:02:31Z] cudaDriverGetVersion() -> 530.41
[2026-03-17T14:02:31Z] libcuda.so: undefined symbol: cuFuncSetAttribute
[2026-03-17T14:02:31Z] nvml Xid 79 at driver 530.41
ERROR: invalid device function
```

sophia: that libcuda undefined symbol + Xid79 pattern screams host/container driver mismatch. CI host driver might be older/newer than container's libcuda.

kai: +1. which base image are we using in the smoke? if it's cuda:12.1 + host driver 11.x you'd see this. Maria, can you paste the runner node info from the failed job metadata?

maria: runner node: h100-bludg-03 (kernel 6.2), host-driver: 525.60, container libcuda: 530.41 — so yep mismatch. PR didn't touch infra.

jack: cool repro. temporary fix: pin the smoke to the compatible image (libcuda 525) or request ops to roll host driver, whichever is faster. For triage, rerun on a node with driver 530.

ops-oncall: I can queue a rerun on h100-canary-01 (driver 530.41) now. kicking it off.

ci-bot: Rerun requested: Build 12345 (h100-canary-01) queued by ops-oncall

maria: thanks — if that passes we'll pin the smoke image and add a quick infra note. If it still fails, I'll open a quick investigation ticket.

kai: also add a note to the nightly matrix to include host-driver variations; we keep hitting these flakes.

jack: low-effort followup: add an assert in the smoke that prints driver vs libcuda early — helps quick triage next time.

maria: good idea. assigning myself to a tiny PR to print versions + add a README note. will report back when rerun finishes. :thumbsup:
